title: How to organize the primary workbench | Garage
description:
The one surface in the house where things get fixed, glued, cut, and assembled.

This is the Primary Workbench in the Garage. About 60-90 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
A bare bench top holding only the vise and the task light, one tray with the current job in it, clamps racked on the rail, and swept concrete visible under the bench.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Clear the top down to bare wood.
Straighten: Give the vise its own corner and keep a full arm's length of open top in front of it, because that is the space a long board swings through.
Shine: Vacuum sawdust and metal filings out of the bench dog holes and the seam where the top meets the back wall, then wipe the vise screw down and put a drop of oil on it.
Safety: Check the bench outlet and the task light cord for nicks, and confirm you can plug the sander in without a lead crossing the strip of floor you stand on.
Standardize: Tape a photo of the cleared bench, vise and task light and nothing else, on the wall directly behind it at eye height.
Sustain: A project is not over when the glue sets.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
The bench ends every session bare except the vise and the task light.
